initiative.title: Schema diagram that shows what the analyses use
initiative.summary: Make the Schema diagram readable on real projects by emphasizing the tables, fields, and queries that views use, while keeping all data reachable.

sources.anchor: 2:19 at least it has all the data there
views read 16 of 139 fields, 4 of 14 tables; 14 one-step queries
relationship view as a separate action; coverage of sources by dashboards
Tables and links rail row, SourceCard hover, sourceUsage.ts, proposeLinks database-only

claims.statement: The diagram must emphasize the data the analyses actually use.
All data stays reachable from the diagram; unused data is quiet, not removed.
A project with no relationships and many pass-through queries must read cleanly.
Tracing, editing, and Add source keep working.
Row browsing belongs to the data explorer (W4), not this initiative.
Byron wants to see how data sources relate, then build a dashboard on a slice; he sees this as a separate action from hovering or clicking a source in the Data rail.
Byron wants to see which data sources the existing dashboards cover. W4 leaves this view to W5 and will link to it.
The diagram first serves two jobs: how tables relate, and what the dashboards cover. The full model is secondary.
Show where each source came from.
Coverage: mark each table with its readers and light up one analysis path in the diagram; a sources x analyses grid is secondary.
Unused tables collapse with progressive disclosure; unused fields matter less.
The Schema button opens the whole project fitted; a per-analysis entry may open that analysis view.
Done bar: one screen of content readable at normal zoom, with no pan or zoom needed to see structure and read labels.
Agents that build a workspace should declare relationships.

conflicts.statement: Resolved: the CI project was written by an agent script (TASK-0091 dashboard.py) that declared one source and one pass-through query per CSV and no relationships. Byron assumed they were modeled.

history.change: Created intent brief, three approaches, and round 1 questions from the TASK-0092 walkthrough.

Took stock of W1-W4 (exploreda 0.6.0). Superseded unanswered round 1 with round 1b.
Recorded round 1b answers: relate + coverage first, provenance, whole-project start, one readable screen.

questions.question: What do you open the Schema diagram for, most often?
How should unused tables appear by default?
How should unused fields inside a used table appear?
What should a one-step Read query draw?
Which outcome would make this not a mess?

rounds.theme: goals and stakes after W1-W4 shipped (round 1b; round 1 superseded unanswered)

questions.question: What is the diagram main job now?
What does built on relationships mean, and should file sources get suggested links?
What does dashboard coverage look like?
How should unused tables, unused fields, and one-step queries appear?
What is the bar for not a mess?

answers: Most important jobs: relating tables (see how sources connect, then build a dashboard on a slice) and a coverage map. Also important: where the data came from. Full model is less important for the first schema viewer.
He assumed the relationships were modeled and is surprised they were not; agents should include relationships when they build the workspace.
Both coverage views are good: in-diagram marking with one analysis lit up is more important; a quick sources x analyses grid is also wanted.
Unused tables are worse than unused fields; use progressive disclosure to expand an unused table.
Open on the whole project. Maybe a schema button next to each dashboard and analysis shows its dedicated view; the single Schema button shows the whole workspace.
The bar: readable at normal zoom without panning, a screen of readable content. Today you must zoom in to read, and then lose the overall structure.

questions.question: Relationships for file sources: diagram suggestions, agent declarations, or both, and in this initiative?
Check: used tables show all fields; only unused tables collapse?
When the used part does not fit one readable screen, what gives?
Per-analysis view and coverage grid: where do they live?
